nodes.ai_summary: Bootstraps firmware startup and initializes core subsystems.

node_notes.led_pd12: This is the onboard LD4 indicator LED wired to PD12, with active-high polarity recorded in firmware/bsp/board.h. The adapter changes its output using LL_GPIO_TogglePin on the configured LED pin.
node_notes.bringup_app: This application owns the cooperative LED timing and button debounce logic and starts it through app_start. It uses the board_io interface rather than accessing STM32 GPIO registers directly.
node_notes.button_pa0: This is the STM32F4DISCOVERY user button wired to PA0, configured as an input by the STM32 adapter. The adapter reads it with LL_GPIO_IsInputPinSet and converts the active-high level to a logical pressed state using board_button_is_pressed.
node_notes.board_io: This platform adapter configures PA0 and PD12, samples the button, toggles the LED, provides milliseconds and waits with __WFI. Its implementation is firmware/platforms/stm32/board_io_stm32.c and it advances the timebase through board_io_stm32_systick_isr.
node_notes.systick: The 1 ms SysTick interrupt supplies the monotonic millisecond count used by LED timing and button debounce. Core/Src/main.c configures SysTick, and Core/Src/stm32f4xx_it.c forwards the interrupt to the STM32 adapter.

node_notes.start: app_start enters the bring-up application after the platform clock setup. It initializes the board adapter and then enters the non-returning cooperative loop in firmware/app/app.c.
node_notes.changed: This branch determines whether the current button sample differs from the candidate state. On a change, the code restarts the debounce interval; otherwise it tests whether the candidate can be accepted as stable.
node_notes.update_candidate: A changed sample becomes the new candidate and its timestamp is reset to the current millisecond count. This prevents a transient input change from being accepted immediately.
node_notes.sample: Each foreground iteration obtains the current millisecond count and reads the logical button state through the board_io interface. The platform implements the clock read and PA0 sample in firmware/platforms/stm32/board_io_stm32.c.
node_notes.init: This step calls board_io_init to enable the GPIO clocks, set the LED inactive, and configure the LED and button pins. The STM32 LL configuration is in firmware/platforms/stm32/board_io_stm32.c.
node_notes.led_done: This is the merge point after the timed LED check, allowing button debounce processing whether or not the LED was toggled. The flow follows the LED timing conditional in firmware/app/app.c.
node_notes.toggle: When the LED interval has elapsed, this step toggles the output and records the current time as the new reference. The adapter implements the operation with LL_GPIO_TogglePin on PD12.
node_notes.update_stable: After the debounce interval, the candidate becomes the stable button state. The current firmware records this state internally and does not emit a separate button action.
node_notes.debounce_due: The condition accepts a candidate only when it differs from the stable state and has remained unchanged for APP_BUTTON_DEBOUNCE_MS, configured as 20 ms. The decision is implemented in firmware/app/app.c.
node_notes.led_due: This branch checks elapsed time against APP_LED_PERIOD_MS, configured as 200 ms in firmware/configs/app_config.h. The elapsed-time condition is in firmware/app/app.c.
node_notes.wait_irq: The foreground calls board_io_wait_for_interrupt, implemented with __WFI, to reduce polling while waiting for an interrupt. The 1 ms SysTick handler advances the time counter and wakes the loop for another iteration.
node_notes.seed: The loop initializes the LED timing reference and candidate button timestamp from board_io_millis, samples the initial logical button state, and starts with stable state false. These variables establish the timing and debounce state used by firmware/app/app.c.

sequence.title: Sequence Diagram
sequence.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Boot as Core main
  participant App as Bring-up application
  participant IO as STM32 board I/O adapter
  participant Button as User button PA0
  participant LED as LD4 LED PD12
  participant Tick as SysTick
  Boot->>Boot: Configure system clock and 1 ms SysTick
  Boot->>App: app_start
  App->>IO: board_io_init
  IO-->>App: GPIO and timebase ready
  App->>IO: Initialize LED timing and button debounce state
  loop Foreground iterations, waking on SysTick
    App->>IO: board_io_millis
    App->>IO: board_io_button_is_pressed
    IO->>Button: LL_GPIO_IsInputPinSet on PA0
    Button-->>IO: Electrical input level
    IO-->>App: Logical pressed state
    alt 200 ms LED period elapsed
      App->>IO: board_io_led_toggle
      IO->>LED: LL_GPIO_TogglePin on PD12
    else LED period has not elapsed
      App->>App: Keep current LED state
    end
    alt Sample differs from debounce candidate
      App->>App: Record candidate state and change time
    else Sample matches debounce candidate
      alt Candidate differs from stable state and 20 ms debounce elapsed
        App->>App: Accept candidate as stable state
      else Debounce interval is not complete or state is unchanged
        App->>App: Keep stable state
      end
    end
    App->>IO: board_io_wait_for_interrupt
    IO->>Tick: __WFI until interrupt
    Tick->>IO: SysTick_Handler calls board_io_stm32_systick_isr
    IO-->>App: Millisecond counter advances and foreground resumes
  end
